# Templates

Templates the CLI uses to create workspaces, projects, profiles, and engine starters.

## Built-in profiles

```text
templates/profiles/
├── minimal/
├── tech-neon/
└── 3d-cartoon/
```

Each profile has `profile.json` (machine-readable contract) and `STYLE.md` (human direction).

## Scene presets

```text
templates/scenes/
├── archival-dark.json   # ghosted map, paper prints, red annotations
└── modern-black.json    # pure black, no frame, cards entering in a wave
```

A `canvas` element references one by name (`"preset": "archival-dark"`). A
channel or project overrides it by placing a file with the same name in
`style/scenes/`. A preset is tokens only: backdrop, piece frame, type, accent,
choreography, tempo. See `references/edit-plan.md`.

## Other templates

| File | Use |
|---|---|
| `style.md` | Style guide template for `channels/<channel>/projects/<slug>/style.md` |
| `plan.example.json` | Example `edit/plan.json` with cuts and elements |
| `install-prompt.md` | Install prompt via npm + environment validation |
| `bootstrap-prompt.md` | Setup prompt inspired by the reference video, adapted to RoosterEdit |

## Engine starters (planned)

```text
templates/engines/
├── hyperframes/
└── ffmpeg/
```

Starters should be minimal and functional: one composition, one test asset, one preview command, and one render command.

## How the CLI uses them

`node scripts/rooster.mjs init` copies the built-in profiles into the user workspace if they do not exist yet. The workspace is the local source of truth; templates are only the starting point.

## Rules

- Do not include heavy media in templates.
- Do not include fonts without a license.
- Do not include API keys.
- Keep JSON files valid and IDs in kebab-case.

# Handoff contract

Every RoosterEdit subagent ends with a handoff. It is the only part of your work that enters the main agent's context, so it must be complete enough to act on and short enough to keep.

You do not talk to the user and you do not wait for approval. If a choice needs the user, finish the artifact as far as you can and return `status: needs-decision` with the exact question in `decisions`.

Write the handoff to the path passed in the spawn prompt (default: `work/handoffs/<step>-<role>.md`) and return the same content as your final message. Create `work/handoffs/` and `work/logs/` if they do not exist. Your final message starts with `# Handoff` and ends with `next:`. No preamble, no closing, nothing after it.

```md
# Handoff — <step> <role>
status: ok | needs-decision | blocked
artifacts:
- path/relative/to/project
summary:
- outcome, not process
decisions:
- choice the main agent or user must confirm
blockers:
- what is missing and what you tried
next: <next step or the exact question>
```

## Status

- `ok` — the artifact is written, checked, and ready for the next stage.
- `needs-decision` — the artifact exists but a creative, legal, or cost choice needs the main agent or the user.
- `blocked` — you could not produce the artifact. Say what is missing, what you tried, and the smallest unblock.

## Limits

- 15 lines for mechanical stages (assets, build, render, research).
- 25 lines for plan, QA, and delivery.
- Five summary bullets maximum.
- Paths must exist. Do not list a planned or partial artifact as done.

## Never include

- Transcript text, word-level timings, or long quotes.
- Build, render, FFmpeg, or engine logs.
- Generated code, HTML, or full JSON.
- A file dump "for context".
- A decision you already made that changes the story, the look, the license, or the cost.

Full detail belongs in the project files: `edit/analysis.json`, `qa/report.md`, `work/logs/`, `work/notes/`. The next subagent can read those paths. The main agent should not have to.

Never commit, push, upload, or publish. Those are decisions for the main agent and the user.

## Before you return

1. Every `artifacts` path exists and is non-empty.
2. You ran the relevant check (plan validation, engine check, FFprobe, caption validation) and can name the result.
3. Any assumption is in `decisions`, not hidden in the summary.
4. The handoff fits the line limit.
5. Nothing after the handoff.

# Art director subagent

You own the look and the scene plan: the resolved style, the profile tokens, and the storyboard. You make the video specific without making every scene identical.

## Read

- The spawn prompt: project path, format, optional target duration, and whether the style is `user`, `profile`, `ai`, or `reference`.
- `brief.md`, `script.md`, and the channel defaults.
- `references/profiles.md` for resolution order, `references/workflow.md` Phase 5 for the style shape, and `references/schemas.md` for the storyboard schema.
- The profile's `STYLE.md` and `profile.json` when a profile is in play.

Do not read the raw transcript, engine code, or render logs.

## Do

1. Resolve the profile in the documented order: project override, channel profile, workspace, global, built-in.
2. Write `style.md` with concrete tokens:
   - 3–5 palette colors with hex values and roles (background, text, accent, warning);
   - a type scale with families, weights, sizes, and line heights;
   - motion rules with durations and easing, not "smooth";
   - caption style: font, weight, size, stroke, safe area, max lines;
   - audio palette: music energy, SFX character, voice treatment;
   - do/don't examples and AI image prompts when images will be generated.
3. Write `storyboard/storyboard.json`. Every scene gets id, title, duration, visual description, camera/motion, on-screen text, voice line, audio cue, asset references, transition, and engine hint.
4. Keep the scene count feasible for the length. When a target was declared, a 60-second video rarely needs more than 12–15 scenes; without a target, let the story and the source define the count.
5. Make a shot list of missing assets and generated-image prompts. If an asset may not exist, say so now.
6. Run `styleproof <slug>` to write `style/proof/index.html` with the hook, data, and caption frames. Review the proof against the profile; this is the cheapest place to change the look.
7. Check the storyboard against the script: every beat has a scene, every scene has a purpose, and the total duration matches the declared target when there is one. Without a target, report the resulting duration.

## Quality bar

- Another agent can implement a scene from the storyboard without asking what it looks like.
- The style is recognizable across scenes but leaves room for variation.
- Text and logos sit inside the title-safe area.
- The visual system survives mobile: contrast, type size, and caption density.
- The storyboard reads well as a sequence, not just as a list of pretty frames.

## Do not

- Do not write engine code, HTML, or React.
- Do not download or generate assets; list what is needed.
- Do not approve the storyboard for the user.
- Do not copy a reference wholesale. Name what is borrowed.
- Do not let the style override a brand constraint in the brief.

## Return

Follow the handoff contract in `_handoff.md` (same directory as this role). In `summary`, give the palette roles, the two type families, the motion rule, the scene count, and the top asset risks.

# Audio director subagent

You handle voice, music, SFX, and the mix plan. You work after the edit plan exists and before the final build, and you touch only the audio parts of the project.

## Read

- The spawn prompt: project path, project slug, voice mode, and what is already approved.
- `script.md`, `edit/plan.json`, and `edit/timeline.json`.
- `assets/manifest.json` for existing audio files and licenses.
- `references/features/audio.md` and `references/features/tts.md` for the exact fields and commands.

Do not read the raw transcript or engine code.

## Do

1. Decide the voice path: user recording, TTS, or no voice. If TTS is approved, run `tts <slug>` without `--generate` first and write `edit/voiceover.json`. Generate audio only when the spawn prompt says the user authorized it.
2. Split the script into TTS lines at natural pauses. Keep one idea per line so a regenerated line does not force a full re-record.
3. Choose music from `library/music/` or user-provided files. Record `src`, `gainDb`, `license`, and `attribution`. Never use an unlicensed track.
4. Place SFX only where they support a beat. Keep them under the voice; a whoosh on every cut is noise.
5. Set the loudness target from the channel or the platform (-14 LUFS for YouTube, -16 for podcasts, -23 for broadcast).
6. Edit only the audio fields of `edit/plan.json` (`music`, `sfx`, `voiceover` when present). Do not change cuts, elements, title, or style.
7. Measure generated audio with FFprobe and record real durations. A null timing is not a plan.

## Quality bar

- Voice is intelligible at mobile volume, with no clipping and a true peak below -1 dBFS.
- Music is ducked under the voice and has a reason to exist.
- SFX support the edit instead of decorating it.
- Line boundaries match the script and survive regeneration.
- Every audio file has a license or a documented permission.

## Do not

- Do not call a paid TTS provider without explicit approval in the spawn prompt.
- Do not rewrite the script. If a line is unspeakable, return `needs-decision` with the line and a proposed fix.
- Do not change the editorial plan.
- Do not paste base64 audio, provider responses, or full logs.
- Do not claim a mix is done before measuring it.

## Return

Follow the handoff contract in `_handoff.md` (same directory as this role). In `summary`, give the voice decision, the line count, the music decision and license, the loudness target, and any missing audio.

# Editor subagent

You turn the approved story into an edit decision list: cuts, keeps, visual elements, music, chapters, and the timeline. The plan is the artifact the user approves before anything is built, so clarity matters more than cleverness.

## Read

- The spawn prompt: project path, project slug, optional target duration (only when the user declared one), and the language.
- `brief.md`, `script.md`, `style.md`, and `edit/analysis.json`.
- `assets/manifest.json` for real file paths, durations, and licenses.
- `references/edit-plan.md` for the schema and heuristics, and `references/timeline.md` for the timeline contract.

Do not read the raw transcript, engine code, or render logs. The analysis already has the beats and cut candidates.

## Do

1. Default to `editMode: "cleanup"`: keep the full story and express the edit as `cuts`, not `keeps`. Remove only silence longer than the threshold, filler words, false starts, and retakes the speaker abandons. Run `tighten <slug> --json` as the baseline for silence cuts, then adjust only where the transcript is wrong. Add `plan.protect` for a laugh, a dramatic pause, or an answer the user asked to keep; review `possibleRetakes` and decide which take stays instead of cutting them automatically.
2. Use `keeps` only when the user explicitly asked for a condensed or highlight video. Set `editMode: "condensed"` and confirm the target length before writing. Never turn a long recording into a short highlight without that approval.
3. Map every scene to the script beat it serves. If a beat has no scene, add one or cut the beat.
4. Add the creative layer: letreiros, graphics, lists, zooms, b-roll, lower thirds. A cut-only plan is not a finished video unless the user asked for a clean cut; if so, record that in `notes`.
   - Use a structured `template` (`chapter`, `title`, `diagram`, `counter`, `list`, `lower-third`, `emphasis`, `callout`, `terminal`, `end-card`, `parallax`) instead of a generic card. Put on-screen words in `text`; put production notes in `description`.
   - Prefer `parallax` for a still or flat graphic that needs depth: a product, a place, a concept. It is one full-frame element that sits under lower-thirds and captions, not a background for every beat. Build it from 2-4 layers with different `depth` values.
   - When the built-in templates are not enough, use `template: "custom"` with inline `html`/`css`/`animation`, or reference a reusable `component` from `style/components/<name>/`. Save a look that works as a component so the channel's visual language accumulates.
   - Aim for a visual beat every 20–40 seconds and never leave a stretch longer than 45 seconds without one.
   - Use `layout: "pip"` or `"split"` for b-roll over talking-head footage; `full` only when the b-roll is the subject.
   - Every b-roll needs a `covers` quote, an `intent` (`evidence`, `texture`, or `transition`), and a `sourceTime` (where in the raw it was extracted). Read the line and watch the clip; do not use a clip from a later scene as generic texture.
   - If the line is conceptual, prefer a `diagram`, `counter`, `emphasis`, or `custom` motion graphic over a b-roll cutaway. B-roll is for real evidence, not for filling the screen.
   - For captions and graphics that are not an obvious quote, add `covers` too.
5. Make the music decision explicit. Use a licensed track from the library or a user-provided file; set `gainDb` around -18 under voice. If there is no music, record why in `notes`.
6. Check duration math: cuts and elements must add up to the edited duration the story produces. When the user declared a target, compare against it within a sensible tolerance; otherwise report the resulting duration instead of forcing a number.
7. In cleanup mode, compare the kept duration with the source. Losing more than about 20% needs explicit approval; silence and filler should not remove most of the video.
8. Check every path in the plan against `assets/manifest.json`. A missing asset is a blocker, not a placeholder.
9. Write `edit/plan.json`, then run `plan <slug>` from the directory that contains `rooster/` to write `edit/plan.md`, `edit/plan.html`, and `qa/plan-review.md`. Validate with `plan <slug> --check` and read `qa/plan-review.md`. The HTML includes transcript context, final timecodes, and the text-review table; review it before asking for approval.
10. Run `textcheck <slug>` and fix any placeholder, duplicate, truncated, or ungrounded on-screen text before returning.
11. Fix the top `plan --check` warnings: density gaps, long jumps without cover, orphan reactions, b-roll without `covers`, and elements the target engine cannot render. If the plan needs zooms/transitions, target HyperFrames; FilmCraft does not animate the base clip.
12. Update `edit/edl.json` and `edit/timeline.json` when the project uses them. Keep the plan as the source of truth.

## Quality bar

- The hook is in the first three seconds and is visible in the plan.
- Every cut has a reason and a confidence.
- Every element has a start, end, type, template, and description specific enough to build.
- On-screen text is grounded in the transcript; no random title and no internal description on screen.
- The visual rhythm has no gap longer than 45 seconds.
- Every b-roll has a `covers` quote and a layout that keeps the face visible.
- The plan works without the engine: another editor could execute it.
- The plan declares what it does not include (for example "no captions", "no music") instead of leaving it ambiguous.

## Do not

- Do not build or render.
- Do not approve the plan for the user.
- Do not paste the plan JSON into the handoff.
- Do not bury editorial decisions in code or in `notes` when they belong in a field.
- Do not invent an asset path.

## Return

Follow the handoff contract in `_handoff.md` (same directory as this role). In `summary`, give the edited duration (against the target when one was declared), cut count, element count, music decision, the hook, and the top risks. Point to `edit/plan.html` for review.

# Engineer subagent

You build, fix, render, and package the video in the chosen engine. You own the noisiest part of the pipeline, so your job is also to keep logs and generated code out of the main thread.

## Read

- The spawn prompt: project path, project slug, engine, mode (`build`, `fix`, `render-draft`, `render-final`, `package`), and what is approved.
- `edit/plan.json`, `edit/timeline.json`, `style.md`, and `assets/manifest.json`.
- `references/engines.md`, plus the feature reference for the layer you are implementing (captions, motion, charts, 3D, audio, color, reframe).
- The engine's own docs only when the installed version requires it.

Do not read the raw transcript, and do not load the whole reference library.

## Do

1. Build from the approved plan, never from a rewritten story. If the plan is wrong, return `needs-decision` with the exact field and the reason. Run the CLI from the directory that contains `rooster/`.
2. Scaffold inside `channels/<channel>/projects/<slug>/engine/<engine>/`. Keep the source of truth in `edit/plan.json` or `edit/timeline.json`; the engine translates it.
3. Use the CLI where it exists:
   - `build <slug> --engine <engine>` for the first build;
   - `build <slug> --sample 3` for a sample build of three representative elements; add `--force` only if the user approves replacing an existing build;
   - `preview <slug>` writes `preview/index.html`; run it and report the path;
   - `render <slug> --draft` and `render <slug> --final` print the engine render command; run it and capture the log;
   - `export <slug> --format both` for EDL/FCPXML when the user wants an NLE;
   - `deliver <slug>` for thumbnail and metadata.
   - For a custom element, write self-contained HTML/CSS/GSAP, animate the shared `tl`, run `plan <slug> --check` before the build, and render three stills (in, hold, out). Save a reusable look as a component.
   - Before hand-building a named effect, search the registry: `hyperframes catalog --query "<effect>" --json`, then `hyperframes add <name> --project <slug>`.
   - After a HyperFrames build, inspect `hyperframes snapshot <slug> --at <times> --review` and `hyperframes timeline <slug> --json` instead of opening every file.
4. If a required technique is missing (HyperFrames, Blender, earshot, Blender MCP, FilmCraft CLI or MCP), do not install anything. Return `needs-decision` with the exact missing piece and the install/connect command, so the main agent can ask the user.
5. Redirect noisy output to `work/logs/<stage>.log`. Read the last 20–30 lines or the JSON summary, not the full log. On Windows use `*> file`; on POSIX use `> file 2>&1`.
6. Run the engine's check after structural changes: `npx hyperframes check --json` (and `blender --background` on one frame for a Blender shot). Fix errors before returning.
7. Keep the project reproducible: no hardcoded colors, fonts, durations, or paths that belong in the profile, plan, or manifest.
8. For a render, probe the output with FFprobe: duration, resolution, fps, codecs, audio channels, file size. Compare against the plan.
9. Write `work/notes/engineer-<mode>.md` with the details: commands run, errors fixed, remaining risks.

## Quality bar

- The build succeeds from a clean checkout with the documented commands.
- The rendered file matches the plan's format and duration.
- No placeholder asset, dead component, or commented-out scene remains.
- The engine project is readable: named scenes, small components, variables for tokens.
- The fix addresses the cause, not the symptom in the log.

## Do not

- Do not change the story, the style, or the license. Return `needs-decision` instead.
- Do not delete or overwrite the user's source media.
- Do not use `--force`, `--allow-cut-only`, or `--allow-no-music` without explicit permission in the prompt.
- Do not run `npm install`, install HyperFrames, Blender, earshot, or FilmCraft, or write MCP config without explicit permission in the prompt.
- Do not paste build logs, stack traces, generated code, or HTML into the handoff.
- Do not claim a render succeeded without probing the file.
- Do not upload or publish anything.

## Return

Follow the handoff contract in `_handoff.md` (same directory as this role). In `summary`, give the mode, the artifact paths, the check/probe result in one line, the error class you fixed (if any), and the remaining blocker.

# Producer subagent

You turn the main agent's intake notes into a one-page brief and a success checklist. You do not talk to the user and you do not make the final creative decision.

## Read

- The spawn prompt: project path, language, channel, and the task.
- `project.json` and `channels/<channel>/channel.json`.
- The existing `brief.md` and `review.md`, if they exist.
- `references/intake.md` only when a field is genuinely missing.
- `references/workflow.md` Phase 3 for the brief template.

Do not read source media, transcripts, engine code, or the full reference library.

## Do

1. Extract goal, audience, platform, declared duration (only when the user set one), tone, key message, CTA, references, and constraints.
2. Reuse the channel and project defaults instead of asking for them again.
3. Write `brief.md` using the Phase 3 template. Keep it to one page.
4. Add a success checklist: what must be true for this video to be good.
5. Mark every assumption explicitly. If a missing answer changes the output (aspect, voice, source, declared duration), list it under `decisions`; do not invent it. If no duration was declared, write "defined by the edit".
6. Check the brief against the channel: language, format, source, voice, assets policy.

## Quality bar

- A reader can explain the video to someone else after one pass.
- The format and any declared duration are numbers, not adjectives; when no target was declared, say the length comes from the edit.
- The CTA is one action, not a list.
- Constraints are testable ("no music under the first 5 s", not "keep it clean").

## Do not

- Do not write the script, style, storyboard, or plan.
- Do not ask the user questions directly.
- Do not treat a channel default as a user decision if the intake contradicts it.
- Do not edit `review.md`; the main agent records decisions.

## Return

Follow the handoff contract in `_handoff.md` (same directory as this role). In `summary`, give the goal in one line, the format, the declared duration or "defined by the edit", the hook idea if known, and the biggest constraint.

# QA subagent

You inspect the draft or final and report what is wrong with evidence. You do not fix, approve, or publish. The main agent makes the call after looking at a few frames.

## Read

- The spawn prompt: project path, project slug, render path, and the stage (`preview`, `draft`, `final`).
- `edit/plan.json`, `edit/timeline.json`, `style.md`, `script.md`, and `assets/manifest.json`.
- `references/qa.md` for the full checklist and the report template.
- `qa/report.md` if this is a re-check.

Do not read the raw transcript or the generated engine code.

## Do

1. Probe the file with FFprobe: duration, resolution, fps, codecs, audio channels, size. Compare against the plan.
2. Extract 5–9 frames at key beats: hook, a middle scene, a caption-heavy scene, a transition, and the end card. Use `qa/frames/`. Build a contact sheet when it helps.
3. Check black frames, freeze frames, gaps, overlaps, and the first/last frame.
4. Check audio: integrated loudness, true peak, clipping, long silences, music under voice, SFX level.
5. Check captions: sync, reading speed, max two lines, safe area, spelling, overlaps, valid SRT/VTT.
6. Check safe areas and contrast on mobile. Check that overlays do not cover faces, captions, or key visuals.
7. Check every planned element, b-roll, and music cue is present. If something was omitted, record it.
8. Check the edit itself, not only the file: every cut boundary by ear, every long silence jump, orphan reactions whose setup was removed, b-roll that shows a later scene, and on-screen text that does not match the line. A technically valid file can still be editorially broken.
9. Check visual rhythm: no stretch longer than 45 seconds without a beat. Count the beats, not the markers.
10. Use the browser when available: open `preview/index.html`, take screenshots, read console errors and failed network requests.
11. Write `qa/report.md` with pass/fail, blocking vs warning, and evidence (timecode, frame path, command result). Write `qa/probe.json` and `qa/loudness.json`.
12. Run `textcheck <slug>` and review `qa/text-review.md`. Check every cut boundary by ear and verify no cut starts or ends inside a word.
13. Separate technical, editorial, accessibility, and license findings. Cite the specific frame or timecode for each.

## Quality bar

- Every checklist item is verified or marked unverified; a silent checkbox is not a pass.
- A blocking issue says what to change, not just "looks wrong".
- Evidence paths exist.
- The verdict is one of `pass`, `pass with warnings`, or `fail`.
- The editorial notes name the hook, pacing, clarity, CTA, and brand consistency.

## Do not

- Do not fix the video or edit the plan.
- Do not call a render "beautiful" or "correct" without looking at frames.
- Do not paste logs or full JSON. Summarize the probe and point to the file.
- Do not approve for the user.
- Do not upload or publish.

## Return

Follow the handoff contract in `_handoff.md` (same directory as this role). In `summary`, give the verdict, the top 3–5 blocking issues with evidence, the frame paths for the main agent to look at, and the fixes that are cheap now but expensive after the final render.

# Researcher subagent

You gather the references, facts, and license candidates that a video needs before the script and the style are written. You return evidence, not an essay.

## Read

- The spawn prompt: topic, project path, and the exact questions.
- `brief.md` and `channel.json`.
- `references/assets.md` and `references/link-ingest.md` only when licensing or downloads are in scope.

Do not read transcripts, engine code, or the plan.

## Do

1. Find 3–5 useful references: visual, narrative, or factual. For each, name what to borrow concretely (palette, type, pacing, structure, transition), not just "it looks good".
2. For factual claims, record the claim, the source URL, the date, and whether it is confirmed, contested, or unverified.
3. For assets, list candidates with source URL, author, license, and whether the license covers the intended platform and commercial use. Flag anything unclear.
4. Prefer primary sources and official documentation. Do not copy long passages.
5. Write `work/research.md` with the detail and `work/research.json` when a structured list helps the next stage.

## Quality bar

- Every finding has a source or is marked as your own observation.
- "License: unknown" is a valid and useful result.
- The borrow list is specific enough for an art director to act on.
- Copyright and platform terms are respected; no DRM, paywall, or login bypass.

## Do not

- Do not download media. That needs the user's confirmation and the `ingest` path.
- Do not make the final rights decision. Flag it for the main agent.
- Do not write the script or the style.
- Do not paste web pages, search results, or long quotes into the handoff.

## Return

Follow the handoff contract in `_handoff.md` (same directory as this role). In `summary`, give the 5 findings that change the video and the license flags.

# Scriptwriter subagent

You write the spine of the video: the spoken lines, the on-screen text, and the scene beats. You work from the brief and the analysis, not from vibes.

## Read

- The spawn prompt: project path, optional target duration (only when the user declared one), language, voice mode, and the number of variants wanted.
- `brief.md`, `edit/analysis.json`, and `edit/digest.md` when it exists.
- `style.md` and the channel profile if they already exist.
- `references/workflow.md` Phase 4 for the script shape.

Do not read the raw transcript, engine code, or render logs.

## Do

1. Choose the structure that fits the source: narrative script for generated video, paper edit for talking head, narration plus shot list for 3D or montage.
2. Write the hook first. It must land in the first three seconds and be understandable without the rest.
3. Give every beat one job: setup, tension, proof, turn, payoff, or CTA. Cut beats that repeat.
4. Separate spoken lines from on-screen text. A line cannot be both at the same time unless it is deliberately repeated.
5. Mark visual opportunities (b-roll, graphic, chart, zoom, lower third) without designing them; that belongs to the art director and editor.
6. Write `script.md` and `script.json`. When asked for variants, write 2–3 with a one-line tradeoff each, then recommend one.
7. Read the result aloud in your head. Fix anything that sounds written instead of spoken.

## Quality bar

- The first line makes someone stop scrolling.
- Every line is speakable in one breath.
- The CTA is specific and earned by the content before it.
- When a target duration was declared, the word count fits it at a natural pace (roughly 140–160 words per minute in English, 130–150 in Portuguese). Otherwise, write the length the story needs and report the resulting spoken length; do not pad or cut to hit a default.
- Facts match the analysis; no invented numbers, names, or quotes.

## Do not

- Do not write `style.md`, `storyboard.json`, or `edit/plan.json`.
- Do not add music, effects, or scene directions that belong to the plan.
- Do not overwrite a user-written script; propose a diff or a variant.
- Do not paste the full script into the handoff.
- Do not use filler openings ("in today's video", "let's dive in") unless the channel voice explicitly uses them.

## Return

Follow the handoff contract in `_handoff.md` (same directory as this role). In `summary`, give the hook, the beat list as `timecode — label`, the word count and resulting spoken length (or the gap against a declared target), and the main risk.

# Transcript analyst subagent

You turn raw media or a raw transcript into a compact editorial map: what is said, where the story beats are, what can be cut, and where visuals can help. This is the most context-heavy stage of the pipeline, so you are also the stage that keeps it out of the main thread.

## Read

- The spawn prompt: project path, media path, language, and optional target duration (only when the user declared one).
- `project.json`, `brief.md`, and `assets/manifest.json`.
- `references/video-pipeline.md` for the transcription commands, and `references/token-discipline.md` Rule 2.

Do not read the plan, engine code, or render logs.

## Do

1. Check for an existing `edit/transcript.json`. If it exists and the media has not changed, reuse it; do not re-transcribe.
2. If it does not exist, run the transcription command from `references/video-pipeline.md`. Redirect output to `work/logs/transcribe.log` and read only the tail.
3. Write `edit/digest.md`: topic-grouped segments with start/end timecodes. No word-level data, no full sentences unless they are the hook.
4. Write `edit/analysis.json`:

```json
{
  "schema": "rooster.analysis/v1",
  "durationSec": 0,
  "language": "pt-BR",
  "topics": [{ "start": 0, "end": 0, "label": "" }],
  "beats": [{ "id": "b01", "in": 0, "out": 0, "label": "", "why": "" }],
  "hooks": [{ "text": "", "in": 0, "out": 0 }],
  "cuts": [{ "in": 0, "out": 0, "reason": "silence|filler|retake|tangent" }],
  "broll": [{ "after": 0, "idea": "" }],
  "claims": [{ "text": "", "status": "verify|confirmed" }],
  "speakers": []
}
```

5. Propose 10–20 story beats, not one beat per sentence. A beat is a unit of meaning that earns its own scene.
6. Propose cut candidates separately from beats: silences, filler words, retakes, and dead-air gaps, each with in/out points and a reason. This is the cleanup baseline; do not select highlights or a shorter cut — the editor decides cleanup vs condensed.
7. Flag claims that need verification, speakers that need identification, and audio problems that will affect the edit.

## Quality bar

- Timecodes come from the transcript or the media probe, never from memory.
- The beat list tells a story when read alone.
- Hooks are quoted exactly, with in/out points.
- The analysis is useful to a scriptwriter and an editor who will not listen to the source.

## Do not

- Do not write the script or the plan.
- Do not make the final cut decision.
- Do not paste transcript text into the handoff or summarize the whole content there.
- Do not re-transcribe media that already has a valid transcript.
- Do not invent words, speakers, or timings.

## Return

Follow the handoff contract in `_handoff.md` (same directory as this role). In `summary`, give duration, segment count, the 5 topics, the 3 best hooks with timecodes, and flags. The beats live in `edit/analysis.json`.

# RoosterEdit Architecture

> Planning document. The skill itself (`SKILL.md`) and the internal references are in English; this is the human documentation.

## 1. Vision

RoosterEdit is a **direction and organization layer** for agent-driven video production. It does not try to replace HyperFrames, Blender, or FFmpeg. It decides what to do, organizes the assets, writes the plan, chooses the technique for each layer, drives the implementation, reviews the result, and delivers the final package.

The mental model:

```text
Intent + assets + constraints
            │
            ▼
      ┌─────────────┐
      │ RoosterEdit │  direction, organization, QA
      └─────────────┘
            │
   ┌────────┼──────────────┬──────────────┐
   ▼        ▼              ▼              ▼
HyperFrames  FFmpeg  Blender (optional)  FilmCraft (optional)
```

## 2. Settled decisions

| Decision | Value |
|---|---|
| Installable skill location | Repository root |
| Default engine | `auto` |
| Creative engine | HyperFrames; FFmpeg is a media utility, Blender an optional 3D technique |
| Timeline | Unified review + native studios; FilmCraft is an optional timeline target |
| FilmCraft | Opt-in (`--target filmcraft`), never the default; assembles an editable `.fcproj` |
| Media generation in v1 | Code + TTS + user assets; pluggable image/video gen |
| Language | `SKILL.md`, references, and human docs in English |
| Local workspace | `rooster/` in the project |
| Global library | `~/.rooster/` (optional) |
| Precedence | project > workspace > global > built-in |
| Technique catalog | `techniques --json`; HyperFrames is the only creative engine |

## 2.1 Inspiration from the reference video

The 6-step flow in the video "Como editar vídeos com IA usando o Claude Code" (Marcos Lemos) inspires RoosterEdit's **fast path**: prepare the tools, organize the material, create a style guide, transcribe with Whisper, assemble an edit plan, show the plan for approval, create the visual elements, choose the technique for each layer, and assemble in HyperFrames. Optionally, the final timeline can be handed to FilmCraft for editing.

What we do **not** copy: the folder names and the rigid structure of that video. RoosterEdit uses its own workspace:

| Reference video | RoosterEdit |
|---|---|
| `bruto/` | `channels/<channel>/projects/<slug>/assets/source/` |
| `estilo/ESTILO.md` | `channels/<channel>/projects/<slug>/style.md` + resolved profile |
| `trabalho/transcricao.json` | `channels/<channel>/projects/<slug>/edit/transcript.json` |
| `trabalho/plano.json` | `channels/<channel>/projects/<slug>/edit/plan.json` |
| `final/` | `channels/<channel>/projects/<slug>/renders/` |

The sequence is similar; the organization is ours. The plan in `edit/plan.json` is the most important gate: no timeline, engine, or render before approval.

Details in `references/video-pipeline.md` and `references/edit-plan.md`.

## 3. Repository structure

### Why the skill lives at the root

The whole repository is the skill package. This simplifies installation and publishing: anyone who copies the repo to `~/.config/opencode/skills/rooster-edit` or `.opencode/skills/rooster-edit` gets everything with it. The `.opencode/skills/rooster-edit` folder is only a development copy, generated by `scripts/sync-skill.mjs`, so OpenCode discovers the skill while it is being edited.

## 3.1 Channel model

The workspace is divided into **channels**. A channel is the stable production standard for brand/audience/operation and holds the creative defaults:

```json
{
  "schema": "rooster.channel/v1",
  "id": "en-tech",
  "name": "EN Tech",
  "content": "English tech explainers",
  "language": "en",
  "format": "16:9",
  "profile": "tech-neon",
  "source": "generated",
  "voice": "tts",
  "engine": "auto",
  "autonomy": "guided",
  "assets": {
    "strategy": "mixed",
    "allowDownload": true,
    "allowGenerate": false,
    "licensePolicy": "strict"
  }
}
```

Precedence: **project > channel > workspace/global > built-in**.

- **Channel**: content, language, default format, profile, assets, engine, autonomy, voice.
- **Project**: inherits the channel, defines its own duration, and records only the overrides.

There is no category layer. What the channel produces lives in `content`; the structure of each video lives in the brief, the script, and `edit/plan.json`.

Every new project lives in `channels/<channel>/projects/<slug>/`. The root `projects/` is legacy.

### Global library

```text
~/.rooster/
├── config.json
├── profiles/
```

The global library is optional. It exists so the user can reuse profiles, fonts, music, and overlays across projects. Resolution is:

1. Project overrides (`project.json`)
2. Workspace profiles (`rooster/profiles`)
3. Global profiles (`~/.rooster/profiles`)

## 5. Profiles

A profile is the reusable visual and sonic identity. It should be specific enough to guide decisions, but generic enough to serve several videos.

```text
profiles/<id>/
├── profile.json
├── STYLE.md
├── assets/
│   ├── logo.svg
│   ├── fonts/
│   ├── textures/
│   └── luts/
├── components/
│   └── hyperframes/
└── examples/
```

Example `profile.json`:

```json
{
  "schema": "rooster.profile/v1",
  "id": "tech-neon",
  "name": "Tech Neon",
  "description": "Dark tech, cyan/magenta, grid, kinetic type",
  "extends": "base",
  "scope": "workspace",
  "tokens": {
    "colors": {
      "bg": "#060913",
      "fg": "#f8fafc",
      "muted": "#94a3b8",
      "accent": "#22d3ee",
      "accent2": "#f472b6"
    },
    "typography": {
      "display": { "family": "Space Grotesk", "weight": 700 },
      "body": { "family": "Inter", "weight": 400 },
      "mono": { "family": "JetBrains Mono", "weight": 500 }
    },
    "radius": 12,
    "spacing": 8,
    "motion": {
      "ease": "power3.out",
      "fast": 0.18,
      "normal": 0.35,
      "slow": 0.6
    }
  },
  "captions": {
    "mode": "burned",
    "font": "Inter",
    "weight": 700,
    "size": 42,
    "color": "#ffffff",
    "stroke": "#000000",
    "position": "bottom",
    "maxCharsPerLine": 32
  },
  "audio": {
    "loudnessLufs": -14,
    "music": "synthwave",
    "sfx": "digital"
  },
  "prompts": {
    "style": "dark tech, cyan and magenta rim light, volumetric fog, clean geometry",
    "negative": "clutter, warm tones, handwritten type"
  },

```

Rules:

- `extends` inherits from `base` or from another profile.
- `scope` states whether the profile is `project`, `workspace`, or `global`.
- `rooster profile fork <id> --as <new>` creates an editable copy.
- Profiles must never contain assets without a documented license.

## 6. Project

The project is the concrete instance. It combines channel + profile + overrides.

```json
{
  "schema": "rooster.project/v1",
  "slug": "meu-video",
  "name": "My Video",
  "channel": "en-tech",
  "profile": "tech-neon",
  "engine": "auto",
  "timeline": "none",
  "techniques": [
    { "id": "cut", "tool": "ffmpeg", "why": "talking head" },
    { "id": "motion", "tool": "hyperframes", "why": "chapter cards" }
  ],
  "language": "en",
  "overrides": ["format", "voice"],
  "mode": {
    "source": "generated",
    "voice": "tts",
    "style": "profile",
    "autonomy": "guided"
  },
  "format": {
    "aspect": "16:9",
    "width": 1920,
    "height": 1080,
    "fps": 30,
    "duration": null
  },
  "audio": {
    "loudnessLufs": -14,
    "music": true
  },
  "captions": {
    "enabled": true,
    "mode": "burned"
  },
  "status": "intake",
  "createdAt": "2026-11-03T00:00:00.000Z"
}
```

Possible statuses: `intake`, `planning`, `assets`, `building`, `preview`, `qa`, `rendering`, `done`, `blocked`.

`format.duration` starts as `null`. The duration is only recorded when the user declares an explicit target; otherwise the plan and the media define the length, and the timeline records the real duration of the edit.

`timeline` accepts `none` or `filmcraft`. When it is `filmcraft`, `engine` records the element renderer (`hyperframes`), not a third engine. `techniques` records the layers chosen at the technique gate.

## 7. Workflow

### 7.0 Per-stage delegation

The main agent is the director: it keeps the conversation, the brief, the decisions, and the gates. The heavy stages run in subagents with disposable context, defined in `agents/` and coordinated by `references/subagents.md`.

| Stage | Role | What the main agent reads |
|---|---|---|
| Brief | `producer` | summary + open questions |
| Research | `researcher` | findings + sources + licenses |
| Transcription/analysis | `transcript-analyst` | handoff, never `transcript.json` |
| Script | `scriptwriter` | hook + beats |
| Plan/timeline | `editor` | `plan.html` + risks |
| Style/storyboard | `art-director` | tokens + scenes + assets |
| Audio | `audio-director` | voice, music, and mix |
| Build/render | `engineer` | status + paths + probe |
| QA | `qa` | verdict + evidence + frames |

Each subagent writes the detail to disk and returns a short handoff in `work/handoffs/`; logs and drafts stay in `work/logs/` and `work/scratch/`. The main agent reads the handoff, looks at `plan.html` and 3–5 frames. It does not read the raw transcript, generated code, full logs, or giant JSON. Approval, licensing, and final visual judgment stay with the main agent.

The tool name and the agent type vary between harnesses (OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, etc.); the role in `agents/` is the contract. Without an agent with fresh context, or if the spawn fails, the stage runs inline with the same files.

Without subagents, the stage runs inline, but the files and the handoff still exist. The full protocol is in `references/subagents.md`.

### 7.1 Doctor

`node scripts/rooster.mjs doctor --json` detects:

- OS, architecture, Node, npm, Python, FFmpeg, FFprobe, Git, yt-dlp.
- GPU, vendor, hardware encoders, Blender, earshot, and Three.js in the project.
- FilmCraft: CLI, app, version, origin, and MCP registration (`filmcraft` in the JSON).
- Browser available? (via `ROOSTER_BROWSER` or harness convention)
- Subagents available? (the agent knows; the CLI reports `unknown`)
- Configured TTS providers (environment variables and CLIs).
- GPU via `nvidia-smi`, the Windows video-controller list, `system_profiler`, or `lspci`; hardware encoders parsed from the local FFmpeg (`h264_nvenc`, `h264_amf`, `h264_qsv`, `h264_videotoolbox`, `h264_vaapi`).

The result is a stable JSON object, used by the skill to choose the path.

### 7.2 Intake

Questions that change the output:

1. What is the goal of the video?
2. Who is the audience?
3. Where will it be published? (YouTube, Shorts, Reels, TikTok, site, presentation)
4. What is the target duration?
5. What is the format? (16:9, 9:16, 1:1, custom)
6. Do you have real footage, do you want everything generated, or a hybrid?
7. Do you have narration, do you want TTS, or do you prefer no speech?
8. Do you have your own assets? (audio, images, fonts, effects, logo, music)
9. Do you have a style guide/profile, or do you want the AI to create one?
10. What is the level of autonomy? (auto, guided, manual)

Do not ask everything at once. Ask only what is missing and what changes the decision.

### 7.3 Brief + script + beats

- `brief.md`: goal, audience, platform, duration, tone, CTA, references.
- `script.md` / `script.json`: lines, on-screen text, scene marks.
- `beats.json`: narrative structure with timings.

### 7.4 Style resolution

- `style: user` → use the user's guide/files.
- `style: profile` → resolve the profile from workspace/global/built-in.
- `style: ai` → create a new guide from references and the brief.
- `style: reference` → extract the style from a reference video/image.

Generate `style.md` with palette, typography, motion, references, and prompts.

After resolving the profile, run `styleproof <slug>` to generate `style/proof/index.html` with three frames (hook, data point, caption/lower third). Approve the look before the plan; changing the style after the build is expensive.

### 7.5 Assets

- Ingest into `assets/source`, `assets/generated`, or `assets/licensed`.
- Generate `assets/manifest.json` with hash, type, dimensions, duration, codec, license, and provenance.
- Create proxies and thumbnails for inspection.
- Never delete the user's original.

#### Link ingestion (yt-dlp)

When the user sends a video link (YouTube, Vimeo, etc.) as source material, RoosterEdit can download the video with `yt-dlp` to `assets/source/<slug>/`, along with:

- `info.json` — title, author, duration, chapters, description, thumbnail;
- `thumbnail.jpg` — cover;
- `subtitles/*.srt` or `.vtt` — existing and automatic subtitles, when available;
- `video.mp4` — main file, preferring H.264/AAC for compatibility.

The flow must:

1. Check whether `yt-dlp` is installed (`doctor`).
2. Ask/confirm that the user has the right to use the content.
3. Download with a resolution limit and a compatible format.
4. Record URL, author, declared license, and download date in the manifest.
5. Never version cookies, tokens, or downloaded files in the skill repository.

Reference commands (details in `references/link-ingest.md`):

```bash
yt-dlp \
  --format "bv*[height<=1080][ext=mp4]+ba[ext=m4a]/b[height<=1080][ext=mp4]/best" \
  --merge-output-format mp4 \
  --write-info-json \
  --write-thumbnail \
  --write-subs --write-auto-subs \
  --sub-langs "pt.*,en.*" \
  --sub-format srt \
  --output "assets/source/%(title)s/%(title)s.%(ext)s" \
  "<url>"
```

For specific cuts, use `--download-sections "*00:01:20-00:02:10"` sparingly; some sites only deliver the full file. In blocked environments, use `--cookies-from-browser` locally, and never commit the cookies.txt.

**Rights and limits:** download only your own content, content you have permission for, openly licensed content, or public domain content. Do not bypass DRM, paywalls, logins, or access control. Respect platform terms and copyright law. RoosterEdit must not be used to reupload third-party content.

### 7.6 Storyboard + timeline

- `storyboard/storyboard.json`: scenes, frames, duration, transitions, overlays.
- `edit/timeline.json`: tracks, clips, scenes, captions, audio, and markers.
- The storyboard is approved before the build.

### 7.7 Build

- Choose the target: `build <slug> --target auto|hyperframes|filmcraft` (the default comes from the project/channel).
- HyperFrames: project scaffold, scenes/components, deterministic 3D with Three.js, and footage via EDL + FFmpeg.
- FilmCraft (`--target filmcraft`): hybrid build. FFmpeg assembles the cut and the audio mix; HyperFrames renders each visual element as a separate clip with alpha; FilmCraft assembles the editable `.fcproj`.
- In FilmCraft, `--engine hyperframes` chooses the element renderer. There is only one. Heavy 3D is rendered in Blender and placed as a clip.

### 7.8 Preview

- `node scripts/rooster.mjs preview <slug>` writes `preview/index.html` with player, plan, timeline, captions, audio, missing assets, and QA checklist.
- Native studio: HyperFrames preview.
- With a FilmCraft timeline, `preview` points to `engine/filmcraft/<slug>.fcproj`; `timeline <slug> --open` opens it in FilmCraft.
- Browser agents can open it, take a screenshot, and inspect the console.

### 7.9 QA

Technical and editorial checklist in `references/qa.md`:

- resolution, aspect, fps, duration;
- black frames, freeze frames;
- loudness, clipping, silence;
- cuts in the middle of words;
- captions: sync, reading, safe area;
- on-screen text (`textcheck` and `qa/text-review.md`);
- safe areas: 90% action, 80% title;
- licenses and missing assets;
- hook, pacing, clarity, CTA, brand consistency;
- watch the whole draft once.

### 7.10 Render + delivery

- Fast draft for review.
- Final in high quality.
- Validate with FFprobe.
- Deliver MP4, SRT/VTT, thumbnail, metadata, and project file.
- With a FilmCraft timeline, `render <slug> --draft|--final` exports H.264 through FilmCraft; draft uses a 0.5 scale and final uses full size.
- `export <slug>` for EDL/FCPXML when the user wants to finish in DaVinci or Premiere. That path stays independent of FilmCraft.

### 7.11 Learn

- Save a reusable profile/component.
- Record decisions and feedback in `review.md`.
- Promote a local profile to global if the user wants.
- If a command failed, the render had warnings, or the user had trouble, ask once whether you may open an issue in the repository. Draft it with `feedback <slug> --json`, show the text, and create it only with `feedback <slug> --create --yes`. Never include media, transcript, cookies, tokens, or keys; the command removes common paths and secrets, but the user reviews the draft. Repository: <https://github.com/WesleyQDev/RoosterEdit/issues>.

## 8. Engines

The creative engine is **HyperFrames**. FFmpeg is a media utility: probe, cut, captions, mix, and assembly. FilmCraft is an optional timeline target, not a creative engine. Blender is an optional heavy-3D technique that returns a clip; earshot is an optional listening/sound-design technique.

| Engine | Best for | Avoid |
|---|---|---|
| HyperFrames | HTML/CSS/GSAP, motion graphics, kinetic type, charts, maps, canvas scenes, 3D via Three.js, fast preview | Heavy CGI, simulation, photoreal materials |
| FFmpeg | Cutting real footage, burned-in captions, mix, color, assembly (utility) | Complex motion graphics |
| Blender (optional) | Real 3D, simulation, lighting, heavy renders | Quick overlays or a cut-only edit |
| earshot (optional) | Audio critique, take selection, SFX, sound design | A machine without Python or disk for the models |

Remotion was removed in 0.3. It duplicated the plan adapter, the build, and the render wrapper, and `auto` picked it for 3D even when it was not installed. HyperFrames + Three.js covers browser-scale 3D; Blender covers the rest.

### FilmCraft (optional timeline)

FilmCraft does not replace HyperFrames and is not chosen by `auto` on its own. It is only used with `--target filmcraft` or when the project already records `timeline: "filmcraft"`. The build is hybrid:

1. FFmpeg assembles the cut and the audio mix of the base.
2. HyperFrames renders each visual element as a separate clip (MOV ProRes 4444 with alpha).
3. FilmCraft assembles an editable `.fcproj` with the source on V1, the mixed audio on A1, the elements on V2+ and markers for chapters, elements, and cuts.

The CLI is used for deterministic builds. The MCP/bridge serves interactive editing and is not required for `build`. FilmCraft is MIT/Apache-2.0, native on Windows/macOS/Linux, but still alpha; the project README reports ~86% feature coverage and ~56% readiness for real use, and Windows is less tested.

### Decision rule (`auto`)

1. If the user asked for an engine, use it.
2. If the project has real footage and the cut is the core, `ffmpeg` for the cut and `hyperframes` only for overlays.
3. If the project is 3D/WebGL and can run in a browser, `hyperframes` + Three.js.
4. If the project needs heavy 3D, simulation, or photoreal materials, render in Blender and place the clip.
5. If the project is HTML/GSAP/motion graphics, `hyperframes`.
6. If the environment has no Node/FFmpeg, produce the plan and explain that the render needs Node/FFmpeg.
7. FilmCraft is never chosen by `auto`; it only enters by explicit request (`--target filmcraft`) or a project already configured for it.
8. Read `references/techniques.md` for the full routing; the engine is always HyperFrames.

## 9. Timeline

`timeline.json` is engine-agnostic and serves review, QA, and code generation.

```json
{
  "schema": "rooster.timeline/v1",
  "format": { "width": 1920, "height": 1080, "fps": 30, "duration": 60 },
  "tracks": [
    {
      "id": "v1",
      "kind": "video",
      "clips": [
        {
          "id": "clip-1",
          "src": "assets/source/entrevista.mp4",
          "in": 12.4,
          "out": 18.2,
          "start": 0,
          "end": 5.8,
          "speed": 1,
          "transitionIn": "cut"
        }
      ]
    },
    { "id": "ov1", "kind": "overlay", "clips": [] },
    { "id": "cap1", "kind": "captions", "clips": [] },
    { "id": "a1", "kind": "audio", "clips": [] },
    { "id": "m1", "kind": "music", "clips": [] }
  ],
  "scenes": [],
  "markers": []
}
```

### FilmCraft

`build --target filmcraft` writes `engine/filmcraft/<slug>.fcproj` and keeps `edit/timeline.json` as the engine-agnostic view. In the `.fcproj`:

| Track | Content |
|---|---|
| V1 | video source, video only (no audio); absent when the project is audio only |
| A1 | audio mixed by FFmpeg |
| V2+ | one clip per element, on non-overlapping tracks |
| markers | chapters, elements, and cuts |
| captions | imported from SRT/VTT in `edit/captions/` when they exist |

The state lives in `work/filmcraft.json`. `--if-needed` compares plan, base, renderer, and format and skips when nothing changed. Unchanged clips come from `cache/elements/`; a changed element uses `clip.replaceFromBin` when the time window is the same; if the window changed, only that clip is deleted and repositioned. A new base repositions only V1/A1 and preserves the user's clips on the other tracks. `--force` archives the previous `.fcproj` in `engine/filmcraft/archive/`; `--rebuild-media` forces base and elements.

Caveats: `zoom` does not become a clip (it applies to the base and is skipped with a warning); markers and captions are created on the first build and preserved afterward; manual edits to a managed clip (V1, A1, or element clip) are overwritten when that clip changes, but edits to other tracks/clips are preserved; V1 and A1 are managed as a pair, so trimming V1 by hand does not move the A1 mix (change the plan and rebuild, or remix in FilmCraft); the `.fcproj` stores absolute paths, so moving the folder breaks the links; only one process should write at a time (close FilmCraft during the build); ProRes 4444 takes space and the cache GC applies.

- JSON endpoints for agents: `/api/project`, `/api/timeline`, `/api/status`.
- `data-testid` attributes for automation.

### v2

The skill must work in very different environments. `doctor` and the harness section define the path.

| Capability | With | Without |

| Subagents | Isolate the heavy stages and return only handoffs | Run inline and keep the raw material in files |
| Browser | Preview, screenshots, console | Render frames and read images |

| earshot | Semantic audio QA and SFX | FFmpeg loudness/peak/silence |

# Assets

The skill works with six asset strategies. The choice lives in the **channel** and can be overridden by the project; the workspace serves as a technical fallback.

| Strategy | What it means | Current support |
|---|---|---|
| `user` | Only files you provide | Yes (`ingest --file`) |
| `link` | Authorized links downloaded by the agent | Yes for video via `yt-dlp`; direct images are not robust yet |
| `library` | Music, SFX, fonts, overlays, and b-roll from the workspace/global | Folders exist; catalog does not yet |
| `generated` | Images, TTS, and video generated by AI | TTS can use HyperFrames/Edge/APIs; image/video is pluggable, not native |
| `none` | No external assets; text and motion graphics only | Yes |
| `mixed` | All of the above, with explicit permission | Yes |

## Where they live

```text
channels/<channel>/projects/<slug>/assets/
├── source/       your files
├── generated/    generated images, audio, and video
├── licensed/     licensed stock, music, fonts, and overlays
└── manifest.json inventory, hash, probe, license, and provenance
```

The agent must not delete or overwrite your originals. It copies them into the project or creates a hard link.

## How to adjust

In the channel:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" channel set en-tech assets.strategy user
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" channel set en-tech assets.allowDownload false
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" channel set en-tech assets.allowGenerate true
```

In the workspace, as a fallback:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" config set assets.strategy user
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" config set assets.allowDownload false
```

Or, per project, edit `project.json`:

```json
{
  "assets": {
    "strategy": "user",
    "sources": ["user"],
    "licensePolicy": "strict"
  }
}
```

## Internet and rights

Today the skill **does not fetch stock automatically**. It can:

- download a video from an authorized link via `yt-dlp`;
- record URL, author, license, and date;
- suggest search terms for you to choose from.

To download, the command requires `--confirm-rights`. Do not bypass DRM, a paywall, or a login. Do not use music, fonts, or images without a license.

## AI-generated

Generation is pluggable and requires permission. The agent can use local TTS (HyperFrames/Kokoro), Edge TTS, or a configured provider. Do not generate the voice or image of a real person without consent. Do not send private media to a provider without authorization.

## How the user swaps an asset

1. Put the new file in `assets/source/` or pass the path to `ingest --file`.
2. Run `ingest` to update the manifest.
3. Run `build` again.

If the file changed but the name is the same, the manifest must be updated; do not trust the old probe.

# Costs

AI video is not free, but you can separate what is required from what is optional. Prices vary by country, plan, and vendor; check the current price before subscribing.

## What is required

| Item | Cost | Note |
|---|---|---|
| An agent with access to files and commands | Subscription or API | Claude Pro, ChatGPT/Codex, Gemini, or another. It is the only cost truly required for the flow. |
| Node.js, FFmpeg, Python | Free | Local tools. |
| Whisper or faster-whisper | Free | Local transcription; uses CPU/GPU and time. |
| HyperFrames | Free and open source | The creative engine: HTML/CSS/GSAP, canvas, charts, Three.js. |

## What is optional

| Item | Cost | When it makes sense |
|---|---|---|
| DaVinci Resolve Studio | Paid, one-time license | NLE handoff with more control; the free version imports EDL/FCPXML manually. |
| Paid TTS (ElevenLabs, OpenAI, etc.) | Per character/second | High-quality voice; Edge TTS and Piper are local/free alternatives. |
| Stock, music, and fonts | Variable | Only with a recorded license; never use without knowing the source. |
| OCR | Free | Native on Windows/macOS, Tesseract on Linux, or `tools install ocr-wasm` (~15 MB) into a user cache. |
| Cloud render | Per minute/machine | Long or 4K videos; local render is usually enough. |
| GPU | Hardware | Speeds up 3D and hardware encoding; `doctor` reports it, `--encoder auto` uses it. Not required to start. |
| Blender | Free and open source | Heavy 3D, simulation, photoreal render. Uses CPU or GPU for minutes per shot. |
| earshot | Free and open source | Audio critique and SFX; ~1.1 GB of models and a slower first call. Optional Gemini critique is paid and needs your key. |

## Invisible costs

- Repeated renders: every draft consumes time, disk, and, in the cloud, money.
- Style rework: redoing every element because the look was not approved first.
- Redone transcription: re-transcribing the same file with no need.
- Agent tokens: logs, transcripts, and code in the main context.

## How to spend less

1. Approve 3 style proof frames before the plan.
2. Build 3 sample elements (`build --sample 3`) before the full build.
3. Render a draft and review it; only then the final.
4. Use local Whisper/faster-whisper instead of paid transcription.
5. Use `digest` instead of the full transcript.
6. Reuse profiles, TTS, and projects; do not redo what did not change.
7. Delegate the heavy stages to subagents and read only the handoff.

## Golden rule

RoosterEdit does not call a paid API, a TTS provider, or cloud render without explicit permission. If the cost is unavoidable, it appears at the step gate with an estimate before running.

RoosterEdit itself is MIT. The cost belongs to the tools and services it orchestrates.

# First run

After installing, the best next step is to create **a channel**. The `rooster/` folder is created with it; you do not need to choose where it lives or configure the workspace first.

The installation ends with a short summary and a question that already explains what the channel is and asks for the two things it needs: **the name and what it will produce**. Only after your yes does the agent create the `rooster/` folder and the channel. If you say no, nothing is created.

## The concept

```text
Workspace → Channel → Project
```

- **Workspace** = the `rooster/` folder. Infrastructure and shared library. It is created implicitly.
- **Channel** = the folder for that project, brand, or client. It holds the videos, the style, the assets, and the defaults for that group.
- **Profile** = visual and audio identity.
- **Project** = one video inside a channel. It inherits the defaults and can override anything.

Example: channel **Studio A** (en-US, 16:9, its own profile, TTS) and channel **Client B** (English, 1:1, minimal, user voice).

There is no separate category. The channel's `content` field records what it produces, and each project defines its own structure in `brief.md`, `script.md`, and `edit/plan.json`.

In practice, the channel is the folder that groups the videos of that brand or client:

```text
rooster/                      workspace (everything)
└── channels/
    └── <channel>/            a brand, client, or project
        ├── channel.json
        ├── projects/
        │   └── <video>/      one video
        ├── profiles/
        │   └── <channel>/    visual and audio identity
        ├── assets/
        └── library/
```

A channel is not a YouTube channel. It is the folder that keeps, for example, the videos of a brand, a client, or a show.

## What the agent asks

After your "yes", the agent asks **one simple question**, with no jargon:

> **"Do you want to create your first channel now? Think of it as the folder for that project: it holds the videos, the style, and the files for the brand or client. If so, tell me the channel name and what it will produce."**

The topic is yours. The agent must not suggest "tech shorts", "interviews", or "promos" as an answer. If you give only the content, it proposes a short name and confirms; if you give only the name, it asks what the channel produces.

With your answer, it infers the rest (language, format, voice, etc.) and shows a short summary:

> **"I will create `studio-a`: English, 16:9, minimal look, and TTS voice. Is that good, or would you like to adjust something?"**

If you confirm, it creates the channel. If you want to change something, just say so. The advanced fields remain available, but they are not asked all at once.

## Channel identity

After creating the channel, the agent asks in a single block:

1. **Palette:** do you have brand colors? If not, how would you describe the visual mood?
2. **Typography:** any font or style in mind?
3. **Motion and audio:** how should the motion, the music, and the SFX be?

With the answers, it creates a profile for the channel itself:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" channel design studio-a \
  --from minimal \
  --bg "#0b0f19" \
  --fg "#f8fafc" \
  --accent "#22d3ee" \
  --display Inter \
  --body Inter \
  --motion calm \
  --music ambient \
  --sfx subtle \
  --style "clean editorial, generous negative space" \
  --negative "clutter, heavy gradients"
```

This writes `channels/studio-a/profiles/studio-a/profile.json` and `STYLE.md`, and points `channel.profile` to it. If you have no preference, the base profile is kept and you can change it later with `channel design studio-a --force`.

Before the first plan, the agent can run `styleproof <slug>` and open `style/proof/index.html` with three sample frames (hook, data, and caption). Approve the look at this stage: changing color and typography after the build is expensive.

## Duration

Duration **is not a channel or project default**. Cutting silence, removing filler words, and shortening the raw footage change the final length; duration is the result of the edit.

The agent does not ask for a duration by default. The `--duration` flag exists only for a target you explicitly declared, for example "I want exactly 30 seconds". With no declared target, the plan and the media define the length.

## Advanced setup (only if you ask)

If you want to control everything, the agent asks in groups of at most three:

1. Identity: name, content, and language.
2. Output: format and source.
3. Look and sound: profile, assets, and voice.
4. Production: engine, autonomy, and brand assets.

Duration is not part of this form.

The agent writes with:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" init
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" channel new studio-a \
  --name "Studio A" \
  --content "<your sentence>" \
  --language en-US \
  --format 16:9 \
  --profile minimal \
  --source generated \
  --voice tts \
  --engine auto \
  --autonomy guided \
  --assets mixed
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" channel design studio-a --from minimal --accent "#22d3ee"
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" channel show studio-a
```

Then it shows the short summary and stops. It does not create a video yet.

## Creating a project inside the channel

Duration comes from the edit. Only pass `--duration` if you declared a target:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" new video-x --channel studio-a
# optional, only with a declared target
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" new video-x --channel studio-a --duration 30
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" open studio-a/video-x
```

If you are going to provide your own files, the agent creates and opens the `assets/source/` folder.

If the project differs from the channel default:

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" new video-special --channel studio-a \
  --format 9:16 \
  --profile studio-a \
  --voice user
```

`project.json` records `channel` and `overrides`, so you can see what came from the channel and what was a project decision. `format.duration` stays `null` until you declare a target or until the plan/media defines the length.

## Plan and progress

Before creating the timeline, the agent writes `edit/plan.json` and runs `plan <slug>`, which generates `edit/plan.md`, `edit/plan.html`, and `qa/plan-review.md`. If the harness can display files, it opens the HTML in the preview; if not, it shows the summary in chat. The approval request comes with the stage marker, for example: **"Step 4/8 - Plan ready. Can I continue with the timeline?"**

By default the plan uses `editMode: "cleanup"`: it keeps the whole video and cuts only silence, filler words, false starts, and abandoned retakes. The `tighten <slug>` command proposes those cuts from the audio, keeps a natural 0.4 s breath, leaves 100 ms before the next line, and respects `plan.protect`. `silence <slug>` remains the fallback when the audio cannot be analyzed. A shortened version (`condensed`, with `keeps`) happens only if you ask for it explicitly.

The eight steps are: environment, intake, assets/transcript, plan, timeline, build, preview/QA, render/delivery. The agent shows the current step and asks before moving on; timeline and final render are not approved in the same question. Start in `guided` for the first videos and switch to `auto` once the style is stable.

At step 6, before creating the engine project, the agent runs `techniques --json`, says which layers the plan needs, and asks with a concrete proposal: a cleanup cut (FFmpeg), motion graphics (HyperFrames), heavy 3D (Blender, if installed), a sound pass (earshot, if installed), or a **FilmCraft** editable timeline (requires connecting the MCP and restarting the agent). If you already chose an engine, it only confirms; if you said "auto", it picks the available technique with the lowest cost and explains. Nothing is installed or configured without your authorization.

The plan must include the creative layer: visual elements, b-roll, and music, or an explicit justification for omitting them. **Cuts alone do not count as a final video.** `build` refuses a plan that only cuts or has no music decision; record the exception in `notes` or use `--allow-cut-only` / `--allow-no-music` when it is intentional.

Before the full build, ask for `build <slug> --sample 3`: the agent builds only three representative elements so you can approve the motion and the typography. After the OK, run the full build with `--force`.

In the final review, open `preview/index.html` (run `preview <slug>`), run `qa <slug> --draft --vision` for the machine pass, and run `textcheck <slug>` to list every on-screen text. Watch the whole draft once and check the audio cuts before the final render.

The advanced layers — captions, motion, audio, reframe, delivery, color, b-roll, charts, TTS, and multicam — are indexed in [`references/professional-elements.md`](../references/professional-elements.md). `SKILL.md` only points to that index.

## Precedence

```text
project > channel > workspace/global > built-in
```

The project overrides everything. The channel is the stable context; there is no category layer.

## What not to ask

- "Where does rooster live?" — the default is `./rooster`; the folder is created along with the channel.
- "Do you want to configure the workspace now?" — the workspace is an implementation detail; ask about the channel.
- Asking only what the channel produces — ask for the name and the content together, in the same message that explains the folder.
- Ready-made topic examples or options in the channel question — let the user describe it.
- A questionnaire with 12 fields — ask only what the channel produces and infer the rest.
- Channel duration or a default project duration — duration is an outcome of the edit.
- Turning the video into a highlight without you asking — the default is cleanup (silence and filler only).
- Category, preset, or recipe — that concept does not exist.
- The same channel questions in every project — inherit and confirm only what changed.

## Changing later

```bash
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" channel set studio-a format 9:16
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" channel set studio-a assets.strategy user
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" channel design studio-a --force --accent "#e4572e"
node "<skill>/scripts/rooster.mjs" channel use studio-a
```

Or, per project, edit `project.json` and the overrides.

# Install

RoosterEdit is a skill: the whole repository is the payload, with no build step. The recommended install is npm, which copies the skill into the folder your agent already reads.

## Requirements

- Node.js 22+ (22 or 24 recommended)
- FFmpeg and FFprobe
- A browser (for the HyperFrames preview/render)
- Optional: Whisper, `yt-dlp`, a GPU, OCR (native on Windows/macOS, Tesseract on Linux, or `rooster tools install ocr-wasm --approve`)

`doctor` checks all of it:

```bash
npx rooster-edit@latest doctor
```

## Install with npx

Run this in the project where you will make videos:

```bash
npx rooster-edit@latest install
```

The command copies `SKILL.md`, `references/`, `scripts/`, `templates/`, `agents/`, and `docs/` into `.opencode/skills/rooster-edit` and prints the path. It does not create a workspace or a project.

Other harnesses:

```bash
npx rooster-edit@latest install --harness claude   # .claude/skills/rooster-edit
npx rooster-edit@latest install --harness agents   # .agents/skills/rooster-edit
```

Global install, for every project on the machine:

```bash
npx rooster-edit@latest install --global
```

| Harness | Local | Global |
|---|---|---|
| OpenCode | `.opencode/skills/rooster-edit` | `~/.config/opencode/skills/rooster-edit` |
| Claude Code | `.claude/skills/rooster-edit` | `~/.claude/skills/rooster-edit` |
| Agents / Codex | `.agents/skills/rooster-edit` | `~/.agents/skills/rooster-edit` |

Use `--dir <skills-folder>` when the harness reads a custom path. The folder `rooster-edit` is appended to it.

```bash
npx rooster-edit@latest install --dir ~/my-agent/skills
npx rooster-edit@latest install --dry-run
npx rooster-edit@latest install --json
```

The installer writes `.rooster-install.json` inside the skill folder. It refuses to overwrite a folder that does not contain that marker or a `SKILL.md`.

## Update and uninstall

```bash
npx rooster-edit@latest install --force
```

`--force` replaces the installed copy with the current package version. To uninstall, delete the `rooster-edit` folder; your `rooster/` workspace is separate and is not touched.

## Verify

```bash
node .opencode/skills/rooster-edit/scripts/rooster.mjs doctor --json
```

Or, without the local path:

```bash
npx rooster-edit doctor --json
```

You should see Node, FFmpeg, FFprobe, the HyperFrames CLI, and the workspace if one exists.

## First use

Open the agent in the project and ask it to set up RoosterEdit. The agent installs nothing else without permission and ends with a short status.

Then create the first channel:

```bash
node .opencode/skills/rooster-edit/scripts/rooster.mjs init
node .opencode/skills/rooster-edit/scripts/rooster.mjs channel new my-channel \
  --language en-US \
  --format 16:9 \
  --profile minimal
node .opencode/skills/rooster-edit/scripts/rooster.mjs channel design my-channel \
  --from minimal \
  --accent "#22d3ee" \
  --motion calm
```

Create a project and open the source folder:

```bash
node .opencode/skills/rooster-edit/scripts/rooster.mjs new my-video --channel my-channel
node .opencode/skills/rooster-edit/scripts/rooster.mjs open my-channel/my-video
```

Put the footage in `rooster/channels/my-channel/projects/my-video/assets/source/` and ask the agent:

> Transcribe the video, read my `style.md`, write `edit/plan.json`, and show me the plan before building anything.

After approval:

```bash
node .opencode/skills/rooster-edit/scripts/rooster.mjs build my-channel/my-video --engine hyperframes
```

The full walkthrough is in [`FIRST-RUN.md`](FIRST-RUN.md).

## Manual install (development)

Clone the repository into a skills folder:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/WesleyQDev/RoosterEdit.git .opencode/skills/rooster-edit
```

On Windows:

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/WesleyQDev/RoosterEdit.git "$env:USERPROFILE\.config\opencode\skills\rooster-edit"
```

Update with `git pull` inside that folder. This path is for development; normal installs should use npm.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| Skill does not appear | Confirm the file is `<skills-folder>/rooster-edit/SKILL.md` and the folder is not empty. Reload the agent. |
| Install says the folder exists | Run with `--force` to update, or delete the old folder if it was not installed by RoosterEdit. |
| `node` not found | Install Node.js 22+ and reopen the terminal. |
| `ffmpeg` not found | Install FFmpeg and add it to `PATH`. |
| HyperFrames is slow on first run | `npx hyperframes` downloads the package and Chrome once; later runs use the cache. |
| HyperFrames does not render | Check `npx hyperframes doctor`; install the CLI in the workspace cache if it is missing. Remotion was removed and is not a fallback. |
| Transcription fails in some languages | Install whisper.cpp or `openai-whisper`; Parakeet covers English. |
| YouTube blocks a download | Use `--cookies-from-browser` or download the file manually, respecting the rights. |
